t: Jerusalem grew from a settlement by the Gihon Spring into a capital and sanctuary city, and was held in turn by Canaanites, Egyptians, Judahites, Babylonians, Persians, Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Muslim dynasties, Crusaders, Mamluks, Ottomans, the British, Jordan and Israel.
It is holy to Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and many of its buildings, from the Temple Mount to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, mark events that each faith tells in its own way.
Its history includes repeated sieges, destructions and expulsions, and the status of the city is still contested in the present.
dyk: By one count, Jerusalem has been destroyed completely at least twice, besieged 23 times, captured and recaptured 44 times and attacked 52 times.
ev: First settlement is established near the Gihon Spring, according to archaeological evidence
The Amarna letters of Abdi-Heba name a city called Urusalim
The Neo-Babylonian Empire captures Jerusalem and burns the Temple
Judas Maccabeus captures Jerusalem and restores temple worship
Titus destroys much of Jerusalem and the Second Temple after a five-month siege
Jerusalem is conquered by the Rashidun Caliphate
The Crusaders take Jerusalem and make it capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Israel takes East Jerusalem in the Six-Day War

f.founded: First settled near the Gihon Spring between 3000 and 2800 BCE, according to archaeological evidence; no founder is known, and the Bible says David took it from the Jebusites around 1000 BCE.
f.where: On the southern spur of a plateau in the Judaean Mountains between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea, in the Southern Levant, claimed as a capital by both Israel and Palestine.
f.known: the First and Second Temples; the Western Wall; the Church of the Holy Sepulchre; the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa; Aelia Capitolina; the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem; the walls of Suleiman; sieges and conquests by many powers
f.today: A city of over a million people whose Old City is a World Heritage Site and whose political status remains disputed between Israel and Palestine.
